title: A Choir for the Visitor
premise: Petra Thornbury, a skeptical urban explorer, maps an unmapped tunnel network beneath the drowned town of Hollowmere and finds a door sealed from the inside. When the excavation crew breaks it open, they release something the town's founders bound with a choir of living voices — and the entity begins claiming singers one by one to complete its own liberation. Petra must learn the founders' ritual, assemble a new choir from survivors who each carry guilt worth confessing, and discover that the binding requires a willing voice to remain behind forever. In the end, Petra — the woman who never believed — chooses to stay as the final note, trading her freedom for the crew's survival and leaving her recordings as the only testimony.
about_author: R. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed records in old mill towns before turning to fiction. Their work draws on forgotten local histories and the quiet horror of towns that chose silence over justice.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She maps storm drains beneath Hollowmere for a client and notices passages that contradict every official survey — older, hand-cut, wrong. Her instruments fail in one corridor that hums faintly, like a held breath. Emotional beat: professional curiosity shading into unease she refuses to name.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Quiet Money
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She researches the town's founding families and finds a pattern: disappearances every few decades, always ruled accidental, always followed by generous donations to the church choir fund. Emotional beat: the first crack in her skepticism — coincidence has a shape, and this shape repeats.

chapters.title: Break Ground
chapters.summary: Crew foreman Deshawn's POV. The excavation crew hits a stone door forty feet below the water table, carved with musical notation, sealed from the inside. His crew celebrates; Deshawn photographs the seal marks and feels watched by his own workers. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into instinctive dread.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, invited down as consultant. She confirms the door was barred from inside — someone locked themselves in with something. The notation matches the humming corridor. That night, all six crew members dream the same melody. Emotional beat: denial beginning to cost more than belief would.

chapters.title: First Verse
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. A young worker, Milo, starts humming in his sleep, then while awake, then without knowing he's doing it. He walks to the door at night and presses his palm to it. The stone is warm. Emotional beat: helplessness as the crew realizes the thing is choosing.

chapters.title: What the Founders Sang
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the county archive she finds the founders' covenant: twelve voices bound 'the Visitor' beneath Hollowmere, and the binding must be renewed each generation or completed by it. The last renewal was 1974. The record ends mid-sentence. Emotional beat: horror of inherited obligation no one consented to.

chapters.title: Milo Sings Alone
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. He wakes at the open door with blood on his lips and no memory of opening it. Inside, he heard applause. He tells no one, ashamed, drawn back like a moth. Emotional beat: the seduction of being chosen — the entity flatters its victims.

chapters.title: The Crew Fractures
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. Two workers quit; one demands they reseal the door with concrete; another, Ruthie, insists they finish the ritual properly because her grandmother sang in the 1974 choir. Loyalty to the dead vs. loyalty to the living splits them. Emotional beat: survival making liars of everyone.

chapters.title: Concrete Won't Hold
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They pour the seal anyway. By morning the concrete is scored from within, five parallel grooves, like fingernails or a tuning fork's tines. Milo is missing. Emotional beat: grief and the collapse of every rational escape route.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. She reveals her grandmother's journal: the 1974 choir cheated — eleven voices instead of twelve, a substitution that left the binding thin. Every disappearance since has been the Visitor collecting interest. Emotional beat: the weight of a debt she didn't incur but owes.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. The remaining crew debates fleeing Hollowmere entirely. Deshawn tries; sixty miles out, the radio plays the melody, and his hands turn the wheel back on their own. You can leave the town; the song doesn't leave you. Emotional beat: claustrophobic realization there is no outside.

chapters.title: Learning the Score
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Deciphering the door's notation with Ruthie's journal, she understands the mechanics: twelve living voices, each carrying a confessed truth, sustained until the seal closes. Truth is the mortar. Lies sung into the ritual are what weakened it. Emotional beat: reluctant conversion — she still doesn't believe in the Visitor, but she believes in the evidence.

chapters.title: Confessions at Midnight
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third among four crew members. Around a campfire above the shaft, each confesses a buried wrong: Deshawn falsified a safety report that crippled a man; Ruthie let her brother take blame for her crime; others follow. Emotional beat: raw, painful intimacy — the ritual demands what the law never could.

chapters.title: The Visitor Answers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the door, the confessions resonate; the stone grows hot and the humming becomes articulate — a voice testing their truths, finding one confession hollow. A worker lied. The temperature drops. Something exhales through the seams. Emotional beat: terror that honesty itself is now a weapon aimed at them.

chapters.title: The False Note
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. The liar is exposed — a worker who confessed to a sin he didn't commit to hide a worse one. The Visitor takes him that night, gently, singing him to sleep. The survivors understand the rules are absolute. Emotional beat: moral vertigo — justice outside any courtroom, administered by something hungry.

chapters.title: Eleven Voices
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. They count: eleven people remain who can sing. The ritual needs twelve. Someone must volunteer to stay behind inside the seal, forever, as the twelfth voice — the founders' original bargain. No one speaks. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Volunteers and Refusals
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Arguments, bribes, tears. One man offers himself and is refused — the Visitor wants a specific voice: the disbeliever whose skepticism thinned the original binding when the founders' own doubter fled in 1911. It wants Petra. Emotional beat: fate disguised as choice.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She prepares recordings, letters, a map of everything she learned — testimony against the town's complicity. The crew descends together to the antechamber, where the door now stands ajar and the dark inside is listening. Emotional beat: grim courage; disbelief finally set down like a heavy tool.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Eleven voices begin the founders' score in the antechamber, each verse anchored by a truth. The Visitor rises to meet them — vast, patient, almost tender, offering each singer their heart's desire to break the line. Emotional beat: climax begins; will tested note by note.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Note
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, final chapter of her living voice. As the seal begins to close, she steps inside, singing her own confession: not that she believed, but that she wanted to be the one who didn't need to. The door seals from the inside, as it always had. Emotional beat: sacrifice rendered as authorship — she finishes the sentence the archive left unfinished.

chapters.title: Aftermath, in a Minor Key
chapters.summary: Deshawn's POV. The crew surfaces changed, bound by shared guilt and gratitude. They testify about Hollowmere's history; some justice arrives, imperfectly. Petra's recordings circulate. The tunnels are surveyed at last — and appear on no map. Emotional beat: mourning braided with relief.

chapters.title: Coda: The Humming Corridor
chapters.summary: Epilogue, distant third person. Years later, a new urban explorer finds a hand-cut tunnel that isn't on any survey and hears, faintly, twelve voices holding one long note — steady, contented, waiting to be needed again. Emotional beat: quiet dread; the cycle endures, but so does the witness.
